take_homes: Default to one agent. Split only when the work needs different access, a different dialect or a different stance. Anyone proposing three agents has to show which of the three applies.
Failures happen at the handoffs between agents, and the course says plainly that nothing in it checks whether the final briefing is true.
An agent that writes a file is a smaller risk than one that sends a message to another system, so approval before sending is the rule.

monday.move: Take one vendor or internal 'multi-agent' proposal and ask whether one well-prompted agent could do the same job.
monday.who: Me, and whoever brought the proposal
monday.when: Next time one lands on my desk, not scheduled
monday.stop_condition: One agent does it as well, or someone shows which of access, dialect or stance applies
monday.blocker: Calendar full of steering groups, and I have not run any of this on our own data

misconception.why: The course said what does not work yet and told me to test the claims on our own files. It also told me to use one agent first, which no vendor says. I still think half of this will blow over, but waiting is no longer obviously the safe move.

one_line: First training in years that told me not to buy more than I need and admitted it can't check its own answers. Prove it on our own data and I'm in.
